newsitem.title: KYRGYZSTAN: Canada's Cameco opens remote Kyrgyz gold mine.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Cameco opens remote Kyrgyz gold mine.

text.p: Canada's Cameco Corp. and Kyrgyz President Askar Akayev opened the remote Kumtor gold mine Tuesday in thick fog and sub-zero temperatures high in the barren Tien Shan mountains.
Kumtor, the largest joint venture in the tiny former Soviet republic of 4.5 million people, has gold reserves of 514 metric tons
"Kumtor has shown a future for foreign investment in Kyrgyzstan," Akayev said. The mine is near Kyrgyzstan's mountainous border with China.

"Kyrgyzstan has not been mistaken in its choice of partner," he said of the joint venture partner Cameco, part-owned by the Saskatchewan government. The remaining shares are listed on both the Montreal and Toronto stock exchanges.
The mining company, better known as a large uranium producer, has invested $452 million in Kumtor.
The big deposit was hidden under a million tons of glacier ice and mining equipment had to be carted up a treacherous mountain road to gain access.

Cameco President Bernard Michel said earlier this year the company had initially budgeted $375 million for the project but had underestimated the cost of transporting personnel, materials and equipment to the site.
The work force totals 1,000 people, 80 percent of whom have been employed locally.
Cameco owns one-third of the mine but has a two-thirds voting stake for the first decade of operations. State-owned Kyrgyzaltyn owns the remaining two-thirds.
"We will pour our first bar of gold later this month," John Kazakov, vice-president of Cameco's Kumtor Operating Company, told reporters.

About 288 tons of gold will be mined using open-cast methods, with production seen at 12 tons in 1997 and 15 to 17 tons in following years, Cameco officials said. Cameco has an agreement with the Kyrgyz government to export its share of production to world markets.

The largest investor in the project was a syndicate of banks led by Chase Manhattan Corp., the Canadian Export Development Corporation, the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Finance Corporation, the private sector arm of the World Bank.
